title: Learning the Inverse Temperature of Ising Models under Hard Constraints using One Sample
claim: Changing a single control parameter shifts a system between ordered, aligned states and disordered ones, illustrated on the same graph.
layout: 2 side-by-side panels, same graph, (a)/(b) captions underneath, no arrows
description: Two panels show the same planar-style graph of about 30 circular nodes joined by straight edges. Each node holds a plus or minus sign for its spin. The left panel is captioned (a) Low Temperature (β=β1). Neighbouring nodes mostly share a sign, so the plus and minus spins form large contiguous domains. The right panel is captioned (b) High Temperature (β=β2). The signs are scrambled and neighbours often disagree, so the pattern looks disordered. The figure is black and white line art with no colour, arrows or numeric data. The eye goes first to the dense graph on the left, then compares it with the right. The difference in spin clustering is the whole message.
caption: Two typical spin configurations over the Ising model at temperatures \(\beta_1, \beta_2\) with $\beta_1 \gg \beta_2$ (equivalently at a lower temperature $T_1$ and a higher temperature $T_2$ where $T \propto 1/\beta$). Each node has spin \(+1\) or spin \(-1\). The left panel shows the configuration at a lower temperature, with alignment producing large domains of positive and negative spin assignments, while the right panel exhibits a more disordered pattern.
abstract: We consider the problem of estimating inverse temperature parameter $Î²$ of an $n$-dimensional truncated Ising model using a single sample. Given a graph $G = (V,E)$ with $n$ vertices, a truncated Ising model is a probability distribution over the $n$-dimensional hypercube $\{-1,1\}^n$ where each configuration $\mathbfÏ$ is constrained to lie in a truncation set $S \subseteq \{-1,1\}^n$ and has probability $\Pr(\mathbfÏ) \propto \exp(Î²\mathbfÏ^\top A\mathbfÏ)$ with $A$ being the adjacency matrix of $G$. We adopt the recent setting of [Galanis et al. SODA'24], where the truncation set $S$ can be expressed as the set of satisfying assignments of a $k$-SAT formula. Given a single sample $\mathbfÏ$ from a truncated Ising model, with inverse parameter $Î²^*$, underlying graph $G$ of bounded degree $Î$ and $S$ being expressed as the set of satisfying assignments of a $k$-SAT formula, we design in nearly $O(n)$ time an estimator $\hatÎ²$ that is $O(Î^3/\sqrt{n})$-consistent with the true parameter $Î²^*$ for $k \gtrsim \log(d^2k)Î^3.$ Our estimator is based on the maximization of the pseudolikelihood, a notion that has received extensive analysis for various probabilistic models without [Chatterjee, Annals of Statistics '07] or with truncation [Galanis et al. SODA '24]. Our approach generalizes recent techniques from [Daskalakis et al. STOC '19, Galanis et al. SODA '24], to confront the more challenging setting of the truncated Ising model.
